correctness.rationale: Keller's published small-polygon bound gives the exact base cases for three through five points. Removing three consecutive entries changes the shoelace sum by exactly one five-point shoelace sum, yielding an induction with coefficient increase one per three vertices. Reversal handles the negative side. Repeated-vertex padding of a multiply traversed triangle attains the bound for every residue class of the list length. No finite experiment is used to infer the theorem.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the least universal signed-area coefficient for arbitrary ordered lists in a convex set. It exactly quantifies the first obstruction highlighted by a current geometry source and gives a sharp reusable baseline for longer shoelace certificates. The result is not claimed to improve the source's covering constant.
